task_description: Second, deeper technical audit of the csgo-checker (CS2 account checker) Electron app after the prior refactoring pass. Analyze architecture first, then produce a structured 9-section audit report covering all 10 domains (security, Electron security, dependencies, error handling, resource leaks, Steam/GC/protobuf validation, testing, architecture, performance, code quality). Then fix ONLY the real, safe issues with justification and regression tests, preserving all rank/XP/GC/matchmaking/protobuf invariants and changing no application behavior. Primary real defect: DOM-XSS attribute-injection in the maps-rating modal (html/js/front.js) where GCPD-scraped map name / skill_group are interpolated into innerHTML alt/title attributes without escaping. Keep npm test/lint/package/audit green after every change.

verification.summary: npm test 143 pass / 0 fail (baseline 133 + 10 new htmlEscape regression tests); npm run lint clean; npm audit 0 vulnerabilities; npm run package (electron-builder --dir) produced dist/linux-unpacked on electron 44.1.0 (Windows target fails only for missing wine - expected, not a regression); no Dockerfile so docker build skipped. Test quality reviewed: test/htmlEscape.test.js exercises the real escapeHtml (helpers/htmlEscape.js) and would fail if escaping were reverted - it asserts the exact C-1 attribute-breakout payload `x" onerror="alert(1)` leaves no raw double-quote (becomes ") and that raw injection is neutralized. Verified in code: the '.show-maps' innerHTML template interpolates only mapNameSafe/skillGroupSafe (escaped) at alt/title/text-node sinks, getMapIconPath still runs on the raw mapName so icons resolve, and the 3 dynamic showToast sites escape login/ret.error while the intentional static-HTML update-link toast is untouched. No changes to EncryptedStorage crypto, GC/rank/XP invariants, protoDecode, or the markdown-it changelog path.
